speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help you, I need to know if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually and if they are worse when you move your head. Also, have you had any recent head injury, fever, or hearing changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

While your description of a constant spinning sensation is atypical for classic BPPV (which usually lasts seconds), the lack of systemic illness, normal hearing, and relief with diphenhydramine suggests a vestibular migraine or early labyrinthitis. Before we proceed, I need to rule out central causes. Can you tell me if you have any history of migraines or if you experience visual changes like flashing lights? Also, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or slurred speech?
